chosen.premise: Kabutops swims faster by folding its razor-sharp sickles and limbs into a more compact shape.
chosen.hook: Its sharpest weapons become its swimming advantage.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Kabutops folding its limbs and sickles inward, shrinking its silhouette as a speed trail appears.
chosen.note: A distinctive, well-supported physical mechanic: Kabutops folds its own razor-sharp weapons to become more streamlined and swim faster.

candidates.premise: Kabutops is thought to have come onto land because the prey it hunted adapted to life there.
candidates.hook: Kabutops may have left the sea because its prey did.
candidates.visualIdea: Follow prey icons moving from ocean to land, then reveal Kabutops crossing after them.
candidates.note: An unusually specific evolutionary mystery with a strong reversal: Kabutops may have followed its prey onto land.

candidates.premise: Kabutops reaches roughly 29 knots underwater, then closes in and slashes prey with its scythes.
candidates.hook: Kabutops can hit roughly 29 knots underwater.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate a 29-knot speed gauge as Kabutops rapidly closes the distance to a prey silhouette.
candidates.note: The exact speed is well supported and easy to visualize, though it is more of a statistic than a uniquely rich Kabutops mechanic.

candidates.premise: Kabutops began adapting for land, but its body changed too slowly and the species went extinct.
candidates.hook: Kabutops was already evolving for land when it went extinct.
candidates.visualIdea: Show underwater Kabutops, then highlight its changing gills and legs before overlaying an extinction stamp.
candidates.note: A strong extinction contradiction, but the first cited entry does not support the adaptation claim; only the Ultra Sun entry directly does.

candidates.premise: Kabutops drains its prey, but the discarded body parts become food for other Pokémon.
candidates.hook: Kabutops turns one kill into food for the next Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the scene between Kabutops draining prey and other Pokémon feeding on the discarded remains.
candidates.note: The ecological twist is concrete and supported, though the premise depends on depicting predation and scavenging rather than a uniquely complex behavior.

candidates.premise: The ancient Kabuto becomes Kabutops only after leveling up to 40.
candidates.hook: Kabuto has to reach level 40 to become this extinct hunter.
candidates.visualIdea: Display a level counter climbing from Kabuto to 40, then snap-transform into Kabutops.
candidates.note: The level-40 fact is exact, but evolution-by-level is common and does not reveal much about Kabutops itself.
